title: Out of Life
essence: A dim high-rise bedroom where a man reads a poem to a back that will not turn around: the EX on the fire escape, vaping, while the haze eats the room left to right and the window slides away from every step toward it. Then two bodies fall past streaking towers with a gap between them that breathes and never closes, through a slow-motion vintage party and a hole in its floor, until the only light left in the film is the vape ember, a blue speck on black.
palette_notes: Night blacks and wet teal come from Naraka stills 22ddf809 (blue vapour bloom over a lit shopfront) and 62b9740c (flooded tunnel, cold light at the end); the steel greys and lit window specks from the hive fall shot 8519865f. The warm amber/gold pair (#c9873a, #e9b46a) is the vintage party's light leaks (a883ad75) and the bedroom's one lamp. #5aa7ff is the suite accent and in this poem it belongs to the vape ember alone: the last light in the film. #2a1a2e is the plum of the party's darks so the ballroom does not go brown.

full_text.line: What we've made we don't want, what we've sold to the world, to ourselves, doesn't exist.
I look for a way out through the hallways, within the drawers and fire escapes, trip
on my own words, falling out of life, and find where you go when you leave.
It was the maze constructed by a tainted love, a known yet unknown pit beneath the quicksands
of the make-believe haven, and hidden in the overnourished forest of escapism that calls
At this age, I'll follow, following the full distance between us almost having it all and
starting anew, to rediscover when love was real.
I failed at protecting you from your own vices, crashing the party of your evilest instincts
to find vibrations that echo in silence, love and hate languages that translate and slow
dripping blood salivating on imminent doubts, fully awakening to our darkest nights.
Pause for a second, a spectrum of fields will thread needles of garments made of sweet memories
and photographs, film and fiction that leave me empty.
With your back faced against me, you offer me a new pursuit of happiness as I stumble
on my own words, landing into the secret of where you go when you leave, and I fall

insights: The EX works because he is a back: one back-of-head card, the bomber's silhouette and the ember carry him. Do not build him a face.
The haze must replace, not dim: paint it opaque and reveal it in a sweeping mask, the way the halfworld swaps dot allegiance. A cross-fade reads as a lighting cue, not a substance.
Put the window on a slider. The single gag of the poem is a destination that recedes; it is cheaper and stronger than any camera move.
In the fall keep the towers at mid value and the bodies at full ink; when the towers had full contrast the fall became wallpaper.
Shoot the party extras soft and on 4s and POET hard and on 2s: the slow motion is the difference between them.
End on the ember alone for a held beat; it is the hand-off to 02's flashing lights.

Atlas: the outside of the window is the Orange Haze under sodium light: paint it in one orange ramp only, and keep the bedroom's teal/blue inside. The window is the warm hole in a cold room; never let teal haze spill outside or orange inside.

Atlas: the halfworld frame foundry/01-04 is already the bedroom's layout (drawers left, door at the vanishing point, cross-mullion window right). Build the set from it rather than from the photographic stills.
Atlas: build the vintage party door card once; 14 closes on it and 01 opens on it, so the film loops through one shared card.
future: The black-tshirt POET pack and his falling cards serve 02 (floating in the black void).
The EX's back-only pack, now proven, carries him through 02, 03, 07, 08, 09.
The tower-strip belt returns for 02's road and 05's ascent.
The vintage party set and couples come back in 14.
The blue ember is the first appearance of the suite accent; 04 gives it to the heart.

atlas.district_language: Two districts, one hard cut. The Orange Haze (scenes 01.0-01.2) is the New Boroughs under low-pressure sodium: one orange wavelength that greys every other colour. In cardboard that means the OUTSIDE of the window is painted in a single orange ramp (#fa8d15 down to #351106) with no other hue at all; brick, iron, planters and figures are only darker steps of the same orange, and the haze is opaque painted card that replaces what it covers, never a dimmer. Inside the bedroom keep the dossier's cold teal-blue TV light so the window is the one warm hole in a cold room; the two must never mix on the same card. Architecture is iron hung on wet brick: switchback fire escapes, a spiral stair with planters in a light well, a catwalk with a glowing kerb far below. The salt line sits at 4/10 of every rail as a pale chalk stroke; cyan seams are rare here and read as alarms, so the only cyan allowed is the vape ember. Never show a close-up outside; outside figures are small silhouettes. The Black (01.3-01.5) has no geography and no line or seam: a black stage, the figure lit alone, and the only architecture is the party's warm leak and the hole in its floor.

staging.name: The reading
staging.shot: 35 mm equivalent locked off from the bedroom door at sitting height. POET card in the left foreground third, three-quarter back, page in hand; dresser with drawers mid-left; TV low on the right throwing blue onto the floor card; the window is a lit orange rectangle in the back third with the EX's back framed in it on the escape. Only the drawers, the TV image and the haze move. Insert: TV screen card swapping chaos images whose reds match the beacons outside.

staging.name: Haze at the window
staging.shot: Slow push from the bed toward the sill that never arrives: the camera trucks in while the window card slides back on its rail at the same speed, so it holds size. Behind the window, the escape (front), the spiral stair with planters in the light well (mid) and the orange haze (back) as three planes; the haze card wipes left to right across the room. EX at the rail, back only, vape cloud card pinned to his head.

staging.name: Off the fire escape
staging.shot: High angle over the rail straight down the facade (forced-perspective brick card converging to an orange gradient). The EX card tips backward over the rail top of frame and shrinks down the shaft on a vertical rig; then POV: haze cards stacked on glass pass upward faster and faster until the last one is black. Hold black for the title card.

staging.name: The fall montage
staging.shot: Top-down on a black ground: POET and EX falling cards face-down, EX always lower and turned away, the gap between them breathing on a slider. Tower slabs with red beacon holes and the escape-screen cards scroll upward past them on two belts at different speeds; screens show drugs, party, TV, phones.

staging.name: Crashing the vintage party
staging.shot: Handheld feel: the whole crowd stack jitters on a soft rig at overcranked (half) speed. Three crowd layers of 1930s couples in grey-gold, a lantern line above, a gel of round leak discs in front. POET pushes through the mid layer; the EX's back appears between two dancer cards and is gone on the next swap.

staging.name: Hole in the floor
staging.shot: Floor level: POET's foot card at the edge of the parquet, the hole a black cut-out in a warm spot pool. Cut to overhead: the parquet card with its trapdoor open, POET drops through and shrinks into black; the party crowd stays at the rim, unaware.

heroes.name: The Severn
heroes.in_poem: the tower he reads in: the high bedroom, the hallway that will not hold still, the switchback fire escape on red brick
heroes.build_as_cards: Exterior: one tall red-brick facade card with punched windows and a black iron switchback escape cut separately and pinned 1 cm proud, so it throws its own shadow. Interior: the corridor as a forced-perspective tunnel of 4 nested door frames (the red hallway) that sits behind the bedroom's hallway door. Nothing breaks; only the bedroom window opens (sash slides).

heroes.name: The Severn's spiral escape
heroes.in_poem: the light well outside the bedroom window: where the haze stands and where the EX drops
heroes.build_as_cards: A vertical light-well flat with the spiral stair as a stack of 6 thin crescent treads on a pole, planters as small green blobs on each landing; haze cards slot between landings. Shot from the top landing, the stack becomes the vertical shaft of 01.2.

heroes.name: The Orange Catwalk
heroes.in_poem: seen only from the window, 30 m below: a glowing kerb line through the haze; its platform end is where the EX stands before the fall
heroes.build_as_cards: Distant card: a curving dark deck with a slit cut along its edge and backlit orange (the kerb). Platform end: a black silhouette card of a railing and struts stopping in mid-air, one tiny figure. No interior.

heroes.name: The Underpass Shadow-Pool
heroes.in_poem: not visited; its black water is the rhyme for the hole in the party floor and the cut into 02
heroes.build_as_cards: Borrow its look for the hole: a black glossy cut in the floor card with a faint reflection of the figures above, nothing else.

transitions.how: The fall is vertical and continuous: the last black after the hole in the floor holds, then a pinpoint of window light grows into a pupil and the camera pushes through it into the child's window of 02. The shared card is the black itself; the Severn's light well is the only place in the city that looks straight down to black water.
Loop: the chrome door of the Arcade (14) closes on the viewer and opens on the vintage party; the party's door card should be built once and shared by both poems.
